business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia – United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force since 2012)
Colombia – European Union Trade Agreement (in force since 2013)

Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York 1958)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation); Ley 1121 de 2006 (AML/CFT framework); Decreto 1679 de 2020 and amending Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficios Finales); DIAN Resolución 164 de 2021 (RUB filing format); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular Básica Jurídica 007 de 2022 (Sarlaft obligations); Superintendencia de Sociedades guidelines for non-financial sectors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Corporate Formation and Legal Representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention 1961) or Consular Legalization if country is non-Hague

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport (all directors, shareholders, UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Office / Civil Registry Authority of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Existence (for corporate shareholders)
Certificate of No Criminal Record (PEP-linked diligence; police certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Police or Judicial Records Department

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Financial Institution Reference Letter verifying source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Bank in the remitter's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or SWIFT bank confirmation if accepted by Colombian AML officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, directors, legal representatives and UBOs against the Colombian Listas Nacionales (SIC/CONPES), OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU/UK HMT sanctions, and INTERPOL diffusion notices; PEP determination under Law 1121/2006 and UIAF typologies; enhanced due diligence for medium-low risk triggers; ongoing monitoring required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rues.org.co (administered by Confecámaras); local Chamber of Commerce portals (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Spanish or may use words from other languages transliterated into Latin script; the S.A.S. suffix is mandatory; names must not be identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; diacritics and accent marks are permitted but may be omitted for search purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Salud (unless authorized by Ministry of Health)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection, submit a 'recurso de reposición' before the issuing Chamber of Commerce with corrected proposed name or arguments on non-infringement; if the Chamber maintains the rejection, file a 'recurso de apelación' to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within ten (10) business days after notification; simultaneously apply under a reserved alternative name to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is partially permissible for statutory registered domicile under S.A.S. legislation, but for a data center colocation business, a physical server hosting address is required for operational licensing and commercial substance; use of a virtual office alone triggers a high tax/AML substance deficiency red flag and may cause loss of tax treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 6% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by DIAN, the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio or the Superintendencia de Sociedades considering its low-risk classification; probability increases to 15-20% if virtual office or foreign-managed operations are detected.

Drafting and notarization of S.A.S. constitution document (when contributed assets include real estate; otherwise private document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign documents into Spanish

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Reporting (Registro Único de Beneficios Finales) preparation and filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 5, 17, 21 and 22; Código de Comercio (Decree 410 of 1971), Articles 110 and 353-372; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 of 2015 (mercantile registry rules); amendments introduced by Ley 2195 de 2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (CCB) and the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) national electronic portal; any Colombian Chamber of Commerce may receive the filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución y Estatutos (private incorporation instrument executed by one or more shareholders, subject to inscription in the commercial registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for S.A.S.; share capital may be nominal (e.g., COP 1,000,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares). Subscription must be fully paid within two years from registration (Article 21, Law 1258 of 2008); payment may be in cash, tangible or intangible assets, or future services. No government escrow account is required; paid-up capital is deposited in the corporate bank account and evidenced by a banking certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [•] S.A.S. — The incorporator, having executed the private incorporation document, resolves as follows: (1) The share capital of COP [•], divided into [•] ordinary shares of nominal value COP [•] each, is hereby subscribed entirely by the incorporator and shall be paid as provided in Article 21, Law 1258 of 2008. (2) The registered office is adopted at [address], Bogotá D.C., and the Legal Representative is authorized to record it with the Chamber of Commerce. (3) [Name] is appointed President and Legal Representative, [Name] alternate representative; a Revisor Fiscal shall be appointed if required by law. (4) The Legal Representative is instructed to obtain the NIT, open corporate bank accounts, and file all registries. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — RUES / www.ccb.org.co (electronic name consultation service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name search in the RUES register of trade names, distinctive signs and existing companies. Submit the requested corporate name and two alternative names through the CCB online reservation module; pay the nominal reserve fee if applicable. The reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and must precede any filing of the incorporation drafts.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternatives
Identification document of the founder or attorney-in-fact
RF/form online application for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the reservation expires, immediately select the next available alternative name and re-enter the online reservation desk before the priority window lapses; no further legal cure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary 1-20 of Bogotá (optional notarization) or direct execution by founders before Chamber of Commerce officials
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the exact corporate name, principal object (data center colocation and related IT services), domicile, capital structure, term, board representation clauses, and S.A.S. statutory clauses. Execute the document before a notary when real property is contributed or when founders prefer authentication; otherwise sign before the registry official. The document must be submitted in Spanish; translations of supporting foreign dossiers require a certified court translator.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation document (estatutos)
Copies of founders' identification documents (passport or cédula)
Notarized power of attorney if signed by proxy
Statement of share subscription and payment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry official raises formal objections, correct the flagged clauses and re-execute signatures; if private authentication is rejected, escalate to notarial protocolization of the same instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration, Form Liquidation and Fee Payment at the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registration window or online S.A.S. Digital Registration Service via RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed Documento Privado de Constitución and the S.A.S. registration form through the CCB virtual filing. Await the fee liquidation (liquidación) generated from the declared capital and selected activities, and pay by PSE/bank deposit/credit card. The registration is effective as of the payment date; the Chamber marks the filing with folio number and initiates the inscription.
required_dossiers: Signed private incorporation document
Formulario de Registro S.A.S. (RUES registration form)
Pre-RUT preliminary information data
Identification documents of the legal representatives
Proof of fee payment (bank or PSE receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection (requerimiento), cure the observations within 30 calendar days through the CCB digital window; if the term lapses, the application is deemed abandoned and a new filing and fee payment are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT/RUT Issuance and Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (through Cámara de Comercio data transmission) and the RUES certificate module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, the CCB automatically transmits the registered company data to DIAN for NIT assignment and RUT confirmation. Download the pre-assigned NIT from DIAN services, verify the RUT details online, and obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal from the Chamber. Correct any discrepancies in the RUT using DIAN's virtual RUT update service.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal pre-issuance voucher
RUT confirmation from DIAN
Identification document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIT or RUT contains inconsistent data, file a correction (nota aclaratoria) with DIAN's electronic services and request re-transmission of corrected registry data within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Paid-up Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Comercial banking entity selected by the S.A.S. (e.g., Banco de Bogotá, Bancolombia or Davivienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account in the name of the S.A.S., present the commercial registration certificate and tax documents, and deposit the declared paid-up capital. Retain the deposit certificate as evidence of compliance with Article 21 of Law 1258 of 2008. The bank will conduct standard KYC assessment for the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
RUT/NIT confirmation
Estatutos and First Board Resolution appointing bank signatories
Identification documents of legal representatives
Proof of capital payment (deposit receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional corporate documentation or rejects a signatory, issue a notarized clarification to Board Resolution No. 1 and re-submit; escalate unjustified blocking to the bank's compliance ombudsman or the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Land-Use Certificate and Building/Occupancy Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Curaduría Urbana (municipal urban planning authority) and Secretaría Distrital de Planeación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo confirming that the metro area, street, and lot allow data center colocation operation. If the data center requires fit-out or new construction, file the construction or intervention license (Licencia de Construcción/Intervención) with the corresponding Curaduría; after completion, request the occupancy permit (Certificado de Ocupación) to activate the facility for colocation leasing.
required_dossiers: Certificado de uso de suelo application
Lease or ownership title to the facility
Architectural and technical construction plans sealed by licensed architects
Appointment letter of the responsible constructor and technical director
Payment receipts of urban planning fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land-use certificate classifies the activity differently, file a recurso de reposición before the same administrative authority and align the colocation leasing model with the allowed zoning category; adjust leasehold premises if restoration is impossible.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá D.C. (SDA) and Curaduría Urbana; outside the capital district, the Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) and the respective municipal urban planning authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Uso de Suelo and Licencia de Construcción for the physical installation, together with Permiso de Emisiones Atmosféricas for standby diesel generators and fire safety certification for the colocation hall.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá D.C. (SDA); for facilities outside Bogotá, the Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) having jurisdiction
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Simplified Environmental Registration (Registro de Emisiones Atmosféricas) for standby generator sets below the full licensing threshold in Decree 1076 of 2015; Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Licencia Ambiental with EIA Report) is required only where continuous power generation project capacity exceeds the licensing ceilings or the project affects protected areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooling wastewater must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L; diesel generators must meet the emission limits (NOx, PM, CO) of Resolución 2534 de 2010; ambient noise ≤ 65 dB(A) daytime and 50 dB(A) night per Resolución 0627 de 2006; UPS batteries and e-waste must be managed as hazardous waste under Decree 4741 de 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) issued by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos after inspection of the facility; structural load and seismic-resistance certification under NSR-10; SG-SST occupational health and safety program registered with the Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL); labor inspector approval for the workspace executed by the Ministry of Labor when applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official taxpayer portal: www.dian.gov.co (Muisca and User Microsoft Dynamics platforms for registration, filings and electronic invoicing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) by private document (or notarial deed if real property is contributed) and register with the Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile through the RUES single registry. Step 2: Upon successful Chamber registration, DIAN automatically assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria); the legal representative must complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) by updating tax classification (CIU 6209), VAT responsible status (Responsable de Régimen Común), and electronic invoicing obligations through the Muisca portal or in person at a DIAN service point. Step 3: If foreign shareholders exist, the S.A.S. appoints a Colombian legal representative and registers the non-resident investor ownership details; the S.A.S. itself is the Colombian tax resident. Step 4: Obtain a digital signature certificate (certificado digital) from a DIAN-authorized certification authority (e.g., Certicámara, GSE) to operate the e-invoicing system. Step 5: Enroll in DIAN's factura electrónica system via direct web-service integration or an authorized software operator/tax technology provider, thereby activating the S.A.S.'s fiscal identity for VAT and electronic reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Colombian S.A.S. is an opaque, tax-resident legal entity taxed on worldwide income at the 35% corporate income tax rate (2025) and is a standard VAT taxpayer (Responsable de IVA - Régimen Común). No pass-through or fiscal transparency election is available for the S.A.S. itself; transparency applies only to certain contractual vehicles such as consorcios and uniones temporales under ET Art. 18.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Colombian law. Available statutory elections include: (1) the Régimen SIMPLE de Tributación (ET Arts. 903-941), an optional consolidated presumptive tax substituting income tax and VAT for small taxpayers with gross income ≤ 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 174 million for 2025); (2) consolidated income tax filing by authorized economic groups under Law 2010/2019 Art. 16 where a Colombian parent controls more than 50% of the subsidiary; and (3) election of contractors to be treated as fiscally transparent (consorcios/uniones temporales), which does not apply to an S.A.S. Companies established within a legally recognized Zona Franca may additionally elect the special 20% corporate rate and special VAT suspension regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - Colombia's national value added tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general economic threshold for VAT registration; any person or entity habitually selling taxable goods or services in Colombia must register as a VAT responsible party (Régimen Común). Taxpayers exclusively selling excluded (non-taxable) items, or small taxpayers with gross income ≤ 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 174 million for 2025) that elect the SIMPLE regime, remain obliged to register but are subject to special rules. Separate mandatory registration applies to non-resident digital-service suppliers, but that does not govern the resident S.A.S.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) is governed by DIAN Resolution 000165 of 2023 and Circular 000016 of 2024. Every invoice must be generated in UBL 2.1 XML, digitally signed, and transmitted synchronously (real-time validation) to DIAN through authorized web services/API before the customer receives the document. DIAN validates tax status, NITs, and arithmetic, then returns the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) stamp and QR code for the invoice. Real-time synchronous transmission is the default from 2025 for all VAT-responsible taxpayers; the asynchronous 24-hour modality applies only to narrowly enumerated small taxpayers. Zero-rated export invoices must also be transmitted electronically, and taxpayers must file periodic electronic information (información exógena) with DIAN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated under ET Art. 481. Services qualify as 'exportación de servicios' at 0% VAT where: (i) the supplier is a Colombian resident or permanent establishment (the S.A.S.); (ii) the recipient is a foreign person without Colombian domicile; (iii) the service is performed from Colombia but is actually used or exploited abroad; and (iv) the exporter completes the service export declaration, retains contract and invoicing evidence, and repatriates the foreign currency. For data center colocation and bare-metal/IaaS hosting, DIAN Concepts (including Concepto Unificado 0016/2019 and subsequent rulings) recognize zero-rating where the foreign client remotely manages and uses the server capacity and the servers remain at the client's disposal abroad; by contrast, local hands-on maintenance, cabling, and managed services physically delivered in Colombia are taxable at 19% VAT as domestic services. The S.A.S. should obtain a confirmatory DIAN concept where the provider also owns the infrastructure, and should file refund requests (Formulario 300) within the first 10 business days of the month following the zero-rated operation to claim the corresponding VAT credit attributable to export activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX) electronically accepted by DIAN customs through the VUCE/SIGLO XXI platform for goods, or the Declaración de Exportación de Servicios filed with DIAN within the first 15 calendar days of the month following the service, applicable to colocation services

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or equivalent carrier document) for physical goods; for remote data center services, the signed commercial contract and a service delivery/acceptance certificate evidencing foreign use or exploitation outside Colombia

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas / Declaración de Cambio por exportaciones) issued by a Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary, evidencing collection of export proceeds within the statutory repatriation term
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects export zero-rating claims to strict Formulario 300 refund scrutiny and retrospective review. If the export requirements are not satisfied, DIAN may assess the omitted 19% VAT, impose the ET Art. 648 'inexactitud' penalty of up to 160% of the tax evaded, charge moratory interest (approx. 1.5% per month), and claw back any refunded VAT with interest for a limitation period that generally runs 3 to 5 years, extended to up to 6 years in cases involving omitted foreign transactions or transfer-pricing adjustments. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, or without Banco de la República authorization, triggers foreign-exchange fines of up to 5% of the unrepatriated amount and may disqualify the zero-rating. Fraudulent zero-rating supported by false declarations constitutes criminal tax evasion under Código Penal Art. 402, carrying 4 to 9 years of imprisonment, accessory fines up to 200% of the evaded tax, and potential asset forfeiture; additionally, non-compliant electronic invoicing of zero-rated transactions attracts per-invoice fines of up to 5,000 UVT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Bogotá, D.C.), jointly enforced with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia under Resolución Externa 1 de 2018 and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a partially convertible foreign-exchange regime. Current-account transactions — including cross-border data-center colocation service fees, bandwidth costs, maintenance charges, and intercompany operating services — may be freely converted and paid through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries without prior authorization. Capital-account transactions require registration with Banco de la República. Inbound direct foreign investment in a Colombia SAS must be reported through an authorized local bank or foreign-exchange intermediary; the corresponding exchange declaration constitutes the legal mechanism for later dividend remittance and capital repatriation. Profit remittances are not blocked by exchange controls but are subject to compliance with FDI registration, statutory financial statements, dividend tax withholding, and DIAN tax-clearance procedures. The practical hurdles are not a prohibition on convertibility but rather fines, delays, and loss of the right to remit proceeds if the original capital entry was not properly registered under the current foreign investment regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The export of colocation and data-center services must be channeled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within the statutory periods established by Banco de la República. For goods, the deadline generally runs from the shipment date; for services, from the date the right to receive payment is perfected. In practice, export proceeds received after the invoice due date must be accumulated and immediately channeled through the local banking system. Once received in a Colombian account, the foreign currency must be surrendered for Colombian pesos unless the company operates a registered compensation account (cuenta de compensación) approved by Banco de la República, which allows holding foreign currency for treasury-approved foreign payments. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% for export receipts not covered by a compensation-account exemption. No parallel-market settlement is permitted.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs, such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, or Mercury-style treasury platforms, are not authorized to provide a Colombian peso bank account or to act as a licensed foreign-exchange intermediary under Colombian law. Their licenses from other jurisdictions do not transfer to Colombia and their accounts cannot receive local ACH credits from Colombian treasury operations. They may be used only as auxiliary non-operational rails for expenses in foreign jurisdictions or as a secondary disbursement wallet. The practical feasibility is Low for serving as the primary corporate bank account; Medium as a supplementary cross-border payment tool if the foreign SAS maintains an FX limit and does not rely on those EMIs for capital calls, dividend repatriation, or regulatory compliance reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Colombian S.A.S. controlled by non-resident shareholders, the opening of a corporate bank account generally requires physical attendance of the legal representative and, depending on the bank, the final beneficial owner at a branch or before a notary public to execute the corporate-powers and KYC documentation. Remote opening is not a statutory right and is not uniformly offered by the main Colombian banks. The most reliable onboarding path requires: (i) the legal representative resident in Colombia or a representative physically present at the branch; (ii) acceptance of a notarized corporate resolution granting banking powers; (iii) presentation of original or apostilled incorporation documents; (iv) certified translation into Spanish; and (v) a live compliance interview. Some banks may grant exceptions for extremely low-risk institutional clients with OECD-resident shareholders, but in-person or notarially authenticated presence remains the default and recommended approach.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders with dispersed or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and bylaws, certified Spanish translation, current UBO declaration under Colombian law, passport copies of shareholders and directors, foreign tax identification certificate, and a board resolution granting the local representative unrestricted KYC/transaction mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial projected account turnover materially disproportionate to paid-in capital and registered business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements for the foreign parent and the Colombian SAS, 12-month treasury cash-flow projection, executed colocation lease agreements or binding service orders with named data-center customers, supplier contracts for server hardware, bandwidth and power, and a board-approved business plan referencing ISIC 6209 / NAICS 518210.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction routing or source-of-wealth concern for inbound capital transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from the remitting entity showing the origin of funds, notarized source-of-wealth statement, shareholder capital subscription minutes, contracts evidencing commercial purpose, and a legal background report for the sending jurisdiction; if jurisdiction is on FATF enhanced-monitoring lists, obtain a pre-engagement independent audit and enhanced due-diligence clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Generic or inconsistent SWIFT reference lines in cross-border wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For capital injections: certified capital subscription resolution and FDI registration form. For service payments: commercial invoice, signed colocation agreement, and the associated DIAN exchange-declaration form. For imports of fixtures and computer hardware: bill of lading, commercial invoice, import declaration or ex-works purchase order, and customs brokerage confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between UBO register and signatory authority in the bank mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of legal representation, current excerpt from the Colombian Chamber of Commerce registry, a board-approved signatory matrix, and a certified shareholder register from the foreign corporate parent proving that the designated signatory is not acting without beneficial-owner approval.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder must send the capital contribution by SWIFT MT103 from a conventional bank account in its home jurisdiction to the Colombian SAS's COP-denominated account held with the chosen Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary. The outgoing wire should clearly identify the underlying purpose as direct foreign investment in a Colombian entity. On receipt, the Colombian bank will convert the foreign currency into Colombian pesos at the TRM reference rate and generate the exchange-declaration code necessary for Banco de la República registration. The Colombian SAS must file the applicable foreign-investment exchange declaration through the receiving bank or an authorized currency intermediary promptly; in practice, the bank operationalises this registration simultaneously or within the term allowed by the central bank regulations. The local company must retain the bank-issued proof of channeling, the foreign shareholder's capital subscription resolution, and the corporate approval for share issuance, and must ensure the RUT and Chamber of Commerce e-certificate confirm the SAS's corporate existence and the share capital actually received.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring operational outflows — upstream bandwidth, equipment leases, software licenses, and cross-border data-center telemetry fees — the primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 corporate payment made by the Colombian bank on behalf of the SAS, accompanied by the underlying invoice or agreement and the correct declaration of reason. For large capital purchases of server hardware, network infrastructure, or managed equipment involving international suppliers, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (commercial L/C at sight) may be opened through the Colombian bank, with the foreign beneficiary's bank acting as advising or confirming bank. Domestic recurring payments from tenants and customers are settled through the Colombian ACH/real-time clearing system (ACH Colombia) in COP, while cross-border tenant invoices in USD may be paid into the SAS's foreign currency account or converted before receipt according to treasury policy. Dividend distributions and capital repatriation are made via SWIFT MT103 after DIAN tax clearances and corporate minutes approving the distribution are presented to the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FOREX outright forwards (Forwards Cambiarios) contracted with authorized Colombian banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in COP/USD for synthetic hedging without physical USD settlement
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between COP and USD for balance-sheet and capital-injection hedging
Foreign-exchange options on COP/USD where the local intermediary is authorized by Banco de la República
Onshore spot transactions executed exclusively through the regulated foreign-exchange market (Interbank / FXD) at the TRM price

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Renewal of Commercial Registration in the Registro Único Empresarial y Social – RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (jurisdictional Chamber of Commerce; e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 31 following the calendar year end (December 31); no extension is granted for renewal of the commercial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal is subject to a 15% surcharge on the assessed renewal tariff; failure to renew for two consecutive years triggers cancellation of the commercial registration and administrative strike-off of the S.A.S. from RUES, preceded by Chamber of Commerce notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Annual Financial Statements (Estados Financieros certificados) approved by shareholders and filed with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (registry copy) and DIAN (tax-supporting record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval by March 31; filing with the Chamber of Commerce by March 31 of the year following the fiscal period ended December 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate filing may trigger DIAN sanctions under Article 651 ET of up to 15,000 UVT (approx. COP 705,975,000 for 2024) or 5% of net equity; failure to file with the Chamber also blocks the annual commercial renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April of the following fiscal year (e.g., tax year Y filed April 9–22 of Y+1, per DIAN tax calendar assigned by the last two digits of the NIT).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine under Article 641 ET: 5% of the income tax payable for each month or fraction of month of delay, subject to a minimum of 10 UVT and a maximum of 200% of the tax assessed; default interest (intereses moratorios) accrues at the official borrowing rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Información Exógena (Annual Third-Party Information and Payment Returns covering clients, suppliers, withholding, and dividend payments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (electronic filing via the DIAN portal; formats 2276, 2277, 2278 and related schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in February following the reporting calendar year; exact due date is assigned by the last digit of the NIT, typically within the window of February 1–February 23.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, untimely filing, or erroneous filing subjects the S.A.S. to fines under Article 651 ET, up to 15,000 UVT for non-submission and up to 0.5% of the amounts misreported (minimum and maximum statutory caps apply).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Actualización Anual del Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (Annual Final Beneficiaries Registry Update – RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, per DIAN Resolution 164/2021 and subsequent amendments; the update must be filed within the calendar window assigned by DIAN (customarily first quarter of each year) following the previous registration anniversary or the latest reported change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely or omitted updates can trigger fines under Article 651 ET of up to 15,000 UVT (approx. USD 3,800 for 2024); persistent non-compliance also raises audit flags and impedes tax-clearance digital certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) under Article 203 of the Colombian Commercial Code when the S.A.S. meets any of the following: (i) total assets exceed 5,000 UVT (2024 UVT = COP 47,065; threshold approx. COP 235,325,000 ≈ USD 58,000); (ii) gross income exceeds 3,000 UVT (approx. COP 141,195,000 ≈ USD 35,000); or (iii) the headcount exceeds 50 employees. Additional triggers include public securities listings, regulated financial-sector activity, or parent-company group audit requirements. A data-center colocation S.A.S. below these thresholds is not statutorily audited but must have its annual financial statements certified by a registered public accountant (Contador Público).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian accounting framework under Law 1314 of 2009: Grupo 1 entities apply NIIF Plenas (full IFRS as instituted in Colombia); Grupo 2 entities apply NIIF para las PYMES (IFRS for SMEs), which is the default for a private S.A.S. operating a data-center colocation leasing business. Lease and rack-space rental revenue is recognized on an accrual basis under the applicable IFRS framework; financial statements must be presented in COP with functional currency assessment.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An annual confirmation of the final beneficial owners must be filed with DIAN in the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF). Any direct or indirect individual holding, controlling, or ultimately owning more than 5% of the shares of the S.A.S. (or exercising de facto control) must be identified. Share transfers, dilutions, and changes in voting control must be recorded in the share register concurrently with the transfer and reported in the annual RBF cycle. The update is mandatory even if there has been no change in ownership; shareholders' meetings that approve capital increases or transfers must authorize the corresponding register amendments and the DIAN information update within the assigned calendar window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva)
Minutes Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)
Official Accounting Books (Libro Diario and Libro Mayor)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 650 per year for registered office domiciliation and commercial agent services in Bogota, Medellín, or Cali, including RUES renewal processing support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 – USD 3,500 per year for a certified independent audit (Revisor Fiscal) when statutory thresholds are triggered; USD 400 – USD 900 per year for a registered public accountant's review and financial statement certification when the S.A.S. is below the audit thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Colombia imposes a general corporate income tax rate of 35% for taxable year 2025. No broad statutory tax holiday applies to data center colocation or bare-metal hosting activities. Certain fiscal incentives may apply only to creative industries (orange economy) or green energy projects under specific administrative regimes, but a standard SAS engaged in colocation leasing is not presumptively entitled to such benefits. The tax base is determined under the Colombian Tax Statute (Estatuto Tributario) with adjustments for inflation (on non-monetary assets) and equity (renta presuntiva) components. The effective rate can be reduced by eligible deductible costs directly related to the operation of the data center, including utility costs, rent, depreciation of servers and infrastructure, and cloud connectivity expenses. The 35% rate is computed on the taxable income determined after deductions and exemptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (formerly Form 410) via the DIAN electronic filing portal – Sistema de Facturación Electrónica and Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos (DILO / MUISCA).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within the term established by the DIAN resolution each year, typically up to 9 months after the fiscal year-end (December 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). The deadline schedule is staggered based on the last two digits of the taxpayer NIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIIU (ISIC) code of the principal activity: 6209 (Data processing, hosting, and related activities) or 6312 (Web hosting; data processing) as appropriate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned SAS, the local entity must report its actual Colombian CIIU code; the foreign parent is not a filer of Colombian Form 210 unless it has a permanent establishment in Colombia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT of the SAS and Razón Social.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the NIT assigned by DIAN; no foreign ID can substitute the NIT for Colombian filing purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue including colocation hosting fees, bandwidth charges, power surcharges, and management services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue from Colombian and foreign clients must be included. Revenues from foreign clients are taxable unless attributable to an export exemption; physical server hosting in Colombia is territorially taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs: cost of energy, lease of facility, salaries, depreciation, maintenance, telecommunication lines, outsourcing, and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must meet ordinary, reasonable, and causally related criteria. Payments to foreign related parties must be supported by TP documentation and beneficial ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, FX losses, and other non-operating outlays.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign related lenders is subject to thin capitalization limitations (30% of net equity or 3:1 debt-to-equity under certain rules) and withholding tax, and requires a TP study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction is allowed for dividends paid or remittances to the parent. Profit repatriation is not a deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 56 (Impuesto a cargo / Renta líquida gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting CIT before credits and net of presumptive income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies the 35% rate. Non-resident shareholders may not claim foreign tax credits on the Colombian return; the SAS itself computes its own tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax prepayments (anticipos) and withholdings that are creditable against final tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include amounts withheld by clients (contract retention at 2% to 11% as applicable) and installments paid throughout the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal losses from prior years eligible for offset, limited to 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may not be carried forward indefinitely; the 5-year limit is strictly enforced. No carry-back is allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 500 (Pagos excesivos o saldo a favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excess withholdings or tax credits generating a refund request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds to non-resident shareholders are not normally granted through the SAS return; the entity may only claim refunds of its own overpayments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax owing per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax owing. Minimum penalty of 1 UVT (approx. COP 47,065 in 2025) for failure to file even if no tax is due. Late payment interest accrues at the effective money market rate (interés moratorio) of the Central Bank (approx. 22%–30% annual rate depending on Banco de la República rates). Inaccuracies may trigger the penalty for 'inexactitud', typically 100% of the omitted tax when the misstatement is detected. Late submission of the sworn informative return (Form 210) can result in automatic cross-checks with third-party information and risk of an official assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% (qualified dividend distribution) / 35% on the portion of dividends derived from non-taxed profit if the entity did not pay CIT at the corporate level. Standard dividend remittance withholding tax (impuesto sobre dividendos) is 7.5% provided the distributing corporate profits were taxed at 35%. If the company distributes earnings that were not subject to corporate income tax, the additional withholding rate increases to 35% (making the total combined levy 37.5%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia generally imposes a 7.5% dividend WHT without a treaty. For treaty countries, the applicant must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, have foreign shareholding duly registered, and file Form 468 or the applicable DIAN format to apply a reduced treaty rate. The relevant DTA (e.g., Colombia-Spain, Colombia-Chile, Colombia-Switzerland) must be invoked through the formal procedure in DIAN's RUT and withholding agent system. Documentary proof of beneficial ownership must be provided. In absence of a treaty, the 7.5% statutory rate is final.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents: statutory WHT 15% (2019 rate) or 33% for payments related to technical services if not specifically exempted; certain technology transfer fees may be subject to 15% final WHT when the payer is a Colombian taxpayer and the recipient does not have a local permanent establishment. Interest to non-residents: statutory 15% on loans (15% for external credit with financial entities; 5% on approved cross-border loans under certain conditions, or 0% for certain official external debt). Treaty rates generally range from 0% to 10% for interest and 5%–10% for royalties depending on the DTA. WHT is final and must be withheld by the Colombian payor at the moment of payment, and reported on the official Form 300 (or the corresponding type of income).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when gross income exceeds COP 1,700,000,000 (approximately USD 0.42 million) or net assets exceed COP 1,700,000,000 (threshold annually adjusted by DIAN) for the fiscal year. The threshold is based on the taxpayer's equity or income under Article 260-10 of the Tax Statute. Additionally, a Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 1380) must be submitted when the gross asset or income threshold is met. A TES (Transacción de Empresas con el Exterior) report is required for any payments to related foreign parties regardless of threshold in many cases.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia applies controlled foreign company (CFC) rules and economic substance requirements for entities positioned as decision-making centers. For a SAS whose only activity is leasing physical racks within a Colombian data center, the entity must demonstrate actual staff, contract management, billing, network administration, and physical presence. If the entity is managed and controlled from abroad, DIAN may challenge it as a transparent or artificial structure (BCA, 'Business Corporation Act' or 'substance-over-form' doctrine). Colombia's ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) are not identical to those in the UAE/Caribbean, but the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under Article 869 of the Tax Statute permits recharacterization of transactions lacking economic substance. The coverage is also informed by OECD BEPS Actions 8–10. For the colocation model, substance is established by: (a) ownership or lease of power and cooling assets; (b) local technicians; (c) incidence of risk from equipment failure; (d) billing in Colombian pesos or equivalent under local contracts. A pure letter-box SAS with foreign control and no local economic activity faces legal presumption of sham and the risk of reallocation of profits to the parent jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting colocation service revenues, falsifying invoices (facturas) without DIAN authorization, or omitting energy surcharges from taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from 4 to 9 years under Law 1819 of 2016 (amending the Criminal Code) plus fines equivalent to 50% to 200% of the evaded tax. Civil liability includes the obligation to pay all evaded tax, interest at 29.9% effective annual rate, and an inexactness penalty up to 100% of the misstatement. The DIAN may also impose 'sanción de clausura' (temporary closure) on the establishment for up to 10 days.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company (Sociedad Fachada / Societé de Apparence)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a SAS with no economic substance and using the Colombian entity solely to route foreign server leases without local technicians, administration, or risk-bearing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 60 and 61 of the Tax Statute, income allocation may be disregarded and all income treated as belonging to the foreign principal. DIAN may impose an income tax assessment at the corporate level and additional transfer pricing adjustments. The foreign parent may become liable for Colombian taxes on deemed permanent establishment basis. In addition, directors and legal representatives may be personally liable for taxes not paid when they knowingly executed sham contracts (Article 794-1 of Tax Statute).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or cryptocurrency payments for colocation services from unidentified foreign clients without implementing a minimal AML/SAR risk assessment, or allowing the data center to be used for illegal server hosting (darknet infrastructure).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SAS license or legal existence is not automatically revoked, but the entity may face asset forfeiture (extinción de dominio) under Law 1849 of 2017 if assets are tied to money laundering. Fines up to COP 6,000,000,000 (approx. USD 1.6 million) under Superintendencia de Sociedades regulations for violating corporate transparency rules. Beneficial ownership disclosures mandatory; omission is punishable with fines against the company and responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Penalties (Ajuste Primario y Sanciones)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare TP documentation or submitting a Form 1380 with inflated or fraudulent intercompany service fees (e.g., charging 30% management fee to a related foreign lessor without evidence of benefit).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 100% of the tax adjustment resulting from TP recharacterization (Article 260-9 of the Tax Statute). In addition, a fine of 20% of the value of the transaction omitted from the TP informative return (minimum penalty of 500 UVT in 2025, approx. COP 23.5 million). Late filing of TP documentation triggers a fine of up to 2% of the aggregate intercompany transactions, subject to caps. The TP penalty is imposed on the Colombian entity, but the legal representative is jointly liable if the omission was intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Falsifying Electronic Invoicing Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not issuing electronic invoices (Factura Electrónica) for each colocation billing cycle, or issuing invoices without the mandatory través de la DIAN's authorization, or failing to report invoices within 48 hours of issuance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 652 of the Tax Statute, a monetary penalty of 10% of the value of each non-issued or non-unique invoice. Additional penalty of 1% of the invoiced value for each day of delay, up to a cap of 90 days. Continued non-compliance can lead to the prohibition to operate commercial establishments and a 'sanción de clausura'. For wholly foreign-owned SAS, failure to issue electronic invoices invalidates the expense deduction in the hands of the client, causing the SAS to lose corporate tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Personal Liability of Directors – Corresponsabilidad Tributaria
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors and legal representatives knowingly signing tax returns with false deductions, approving profit distributions while withholding tax is not remitted to DIAN, or allowing the entity to be used for illegitimate tax footballing with foreign related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 794-1 of the Tax Statute, the legal representative is jointly and severally liable for tax penalties and unpaid taxes if they participated in the infraction. The directors' assets may be seized (embargo) for debts of the SAS if fraud is proven. Travel bans (prohibición de salida del país) can be imposed for tax debts exceeding a threshold (over 100 monthly minimum wages). Criminal imprisonment of 3 to 8 years for fraudulent bankruptcy or concealment of assets is possible. In addition, the Superintendencia de Sociedades may order dissolution of the SAS and liquidation if it is deemed to exist merely to evade taxes.
